description: Publication-quality figures for Python, built for coding agents: one-call charts, measured layout and SVG/PDF output.
rules: Make a chart in one call: i.line(df, x='time', y='signal', color='group'); df may be a DataFrame, a dict of columns, a list of row dicts or a CSV path.
Use the one-call functions (i.line, i.scatter, i.bar, i.hist, i.boxplot, i.heatmap, ...) and chart.line(...) etc. to layer on an existing chart; combine panels with | and /.
Bars sum rows that share an x value and warn ROWS_COMBINED unless agg='sum' is passed; for replicates use i.bar(df, x=, y=, agg='mean', error_y='sem').
Text is not mathtext: write x^{2}, H_{2}O or Unicode (x²). $...$ prints the dollar signs.
Sizes are millimetres: width='single' (89 mm), 'double' (183 mm), 'slide' or a number; font sizes are points via i.pt(8).
After saving, figure = chart.save('fig.pdf', 'fig.png') then print(figure.report()); fix every finding it lists, since a clean report means no layout problems.
Run inklet check --json script.py to build a script and get its layout problems as data, and open the PNG preview: a clean check is not a visual review.
i.box is a diagram box, not a box plot (use i.boxplot); significance brackets are chart.brackets([...]); do not call plt.show().
